disclaimer: These are simulated-persona reviews generated by AI agents, not interviews with real coaches. They supplement rather than replace human feedback.
expectations: I expect to go from a proposed film cut to a scouting tendency with its sample and exclusions, then put something I can defend into the weekly plan.
This reads like one school's invited staff. I can see an offensive coordinator using the unit plan and an assistant correcting what the camera actually showed.
In ten minutes I'd expect to be checking one opponent tendency against its snaps before I put it on Monday's install list.

interview.answer: I could see my Westmoor week in one place, but I lost a Monday objective between the draft screen and the approved copy.

Part of it did. Westmoor’s defense cards gave me fractions and review status just as the landing page promised. When I tried to check 10:40, the player stopped at six seconds, and I could find no weekly-plan recommendation to review.

Saturday I cut our tape, Sunday I break down the opponent, Monday I install, and Wednesday I sign the plan. The defense comparison and section comments fit Sunday and Monday. I would still use Hudl to check the front and read back the saved version before I gave staff the Wednesday call sheet.

I selected Their defense because I call offense. Going straight to Plans opened our defense plan and told me I could only comment. I had to switch back to Offense. I also had to remove and add a protection sentence just to change the wording.

I trusted the claim that somebody had corrected play 2 because the panel showed both trips_left and the doubles correction. Confidence alone would never settle receiver spacing for me. I set the 4-of-9 safety rotation aside when the screen said the far safety was outside the frame. The 8-of-13 pressure card gave me no snap I could open to decide whether to teach it.
If the approved call sheet can drop the last adjustment I made, I would stop using it as the staff copy. I saw that happen to the third objective on v3.
First, make approval cover the exact saved content on the screen. Second, let me open the snaps behind a recommendation, then record my accept, edit, reject or defer decision next to the draft.
Keep the numerator, denominator and review-basis tag on the same scouting card. Keep the separate uncertain section and the version and section labels on the staff comments.

My answer on in-season use is conditional. I would use the scouting and draft-comment screens alongside film I can verify in Hudl. My answer on recommending this build for staff sign-off is no. I would reconsider when Approve waits for me to save my last adjustment and I can check each weekly suggestion against its snaps before recording my decision.

The staff roster tells me who owns offense, and the disabled retention field tells me who owns film policy. I would like that same clarity about exactly which version of my words everyone is about to teach.

findings.title: Approve can discard an unsaved objective
findings.element: Save draft, Submit for review and Approve v3
findings.observed: In the mock UI, adding a third objective to v3 disabled Submit for review and left Approve v3 active. Clicking Approve superseded v2. The approved v3 reopened with two objectives and no added Monday instruction. C6 captures the reopened version.
findings.expected: The coordinator should be able to verify that the immutable version contains every displayed edit before approving it.
findings.proposed_change: Disable approval while the draft has unsaved edits and require the saved version to enter review before sign-off.
findings.quote: My staff got an approved plan with the last call missing.

findings.title: Weekly recommendations have no generation or decision controls
findings.element: Offense draft actions and plan sections
findings.observed: The offensive coordinator looked through Plans, Dashboard, Scouting and Playbook. None offered generation or an accept, edit, reject or defer action for a unit-plan recommendation. Source review shows the plan page assembles manual section editors and comments at apps/web/src/pages/PlansPage.tsx:236. The prototype practice focus is a different task.
findings.expected: The coordinator should be able to check supporting snaps and decide what enters the offensive draft through the workflow in contract §15.3.
findings.proposed_change: Add the generation entry point and a review panel with evidence, counts and four explicit decisions for each unit-plan suggestion.
findings.quote: Show me the suggestion and its snaps, then let me tell the staff what I kept.

findings.title: The mock’s reviewed scouting sample exceeds the plays on its source film
findings.element: What this report is built from and the first-down trips finding
findings.observed: The Westmoor offense view described 54 reviewed snaps and linked one film containing 48 plays. Its headline said findings are recomputed from stored labels. Source review confirmed that the mock filters precomputed fixtures and derives its sample header from the largest stored finding at apps/web/src/api/mock/index.ts:766.
findings.expected: A staff member should be able to reconcile the stated sample with the eligible snaps on the listed films.
findings.proposed_change: Calculate mock scouting samples and findings from the same reviewed segments the film links expose.
findings.quote: Where are the other six snaps I am being asked to count?

findings.title: The linked evidence time opens at the end of a substitute clip
findings.element: 10:40 evidence link, selected play and video transport
findings.observed: The even-front finding’s 10:40 link reached the expected asset and selected play 5 at 10:34–10:41. The media transport was at 0:06 of 0:06. The screen disclosed the substitute clip, and the cited defensive alignment could not be inspected in this mock session.
findings.expected: The coordinator should be able to see the cited alignment on the selected snap before using the tendency for install.
findings.proposed_change: Pair each demo finding with a playable excerpt of its cited snap and map original-film timestamps onto that excerpt.
findings.quote: The play number is there. I still cannot show the front to my guards.

findings.title: The fifth-rusher and off-corner findings lack supporting-film links
findings.element: Westmoor defensive strength and weakness cards
findings.observed: The 8-of-13 fifth-rusher card in the mixed view had no timestamp. The reviewed 14-of-22 off-corner card supplied only the contrary 85:20 goal-line example. Both had usable denominators, but neither let the coordinator inspect a supporting example from the card.
findings.expected: A pressure or coverage tendency used to change the call sheet should lead to at least one supporting play or explain the evidence gap.
findings.proposed_change: Expose supporting snaps on each actionable tendency and state when only contrary or unreviewed evidence is available.
findings.quote: Press at the goal line is a useful exception. Show me one of the fourteen off-corner snaps too.

findings.title: Playbook extraction approval offers the OCR excerpt without its source page
findings.element: Sprint-out Smash, Source: page 4 and the red-zone document title
findings.observed: The page-4 citation and document title were static when clicked. Approve moved Sprint-out Smash to Approved, yet its description continued to say the OCR text was unreviewed. The original diagram was unavailable at the moment of sign-off.
findings.expected: The approving coordinator should be able to compare the proposed concept with the original installation page and see its current review state.
findings.proposed_change: Link each extraction citation to the source page and show the current review state after a decision.
findings.quote: I want the original drawing beside that OCR line when I approve it.

findings.title: Rewording a plan item requires deleting and recreating it
findings.element: Protections item text, Remove and Add to Protections
findings.observed: Clicking the existing protection sentence offered no edit. The coordinator removed it and added a replacement to the same section. Source review at apps/web/src/pages/PlansPage.tsx:38 shows that adding creates a fresh item with empty concept and package references and no source recommendation.
findings.expected: A wording change should retain the plan item’s identity and supporting references.
findings.proposed_change: Provide an in-place edit action that saves revised text on the same item.
findings.quote: I changed how I teach the protection. I should be able to keep the same line on the plan.

findings.title: Open plan comments have no resolution action
findings.observed: The in-review version displayed three open comments and one older comment labeled resolved. The panel offered posting and section selection, with no visible Resolve action. The normal v2 approval succeeded while the instruction to hold the uncertain safety item was still open.
findings.expected: Staff should be able to record that an install question has been answered before the coordinator signs the plan.
findings.proposed_change: Add a per-comment resolution action and show the open count at the approval control.
findings.quote: I can ask about the fifth rusher, but I need somewhere to say we checked it.

findings.title: Back from a scouting timestamp changes the review basis
findings.element: Include unreviewed (model) labels after browser Back
findings.observed: The coordinator followed the even-front timestamp from the mixed defense report. Returning with Back selected Reviewed labels only, hiding the 8-of-13 pressure finding and the uncertain safety card.
findings.expected: Returning from film should restore the scouting view that supplied the evidence link.
findings.proposed_change: Persist the review-basis selection in the scouting URL so history navigation restores the same report.
findings.quote: I went out for one snap and came back to a different scouting list.

findings.title: The newest seeded upload has no proposed plays to inspect
findings.element: Caldwell asset, processing jobs and No plays proposed yet
findings.observed: The newest upload stayed at 38 of about 100 minutes scanned across polling intervals in this session. The coordinator switched to the older ready file to inspect a proposed cut. Source review at apps/web/src/api/mock/index.ts:265 indicates the polling simulation advances only designated simulated jobs.
findings.expected: The demo should make it evident where a coach can inspect proposals while the newest film is still processing.
findings.proposed_change: Link the processing asset’s empty timeline to the most recent game film with available proposals.
findings.quote: If this tape is still cutting, point me to one I can work on tonight.

findings.title: Scouting their defense opens the staff’s defensive plan
findings.element: Unit tab selected after opponent-unit navigation
findings.observed: Selecting Their defense in opponent scouting carried unit=defense into Weekly Game Plans. The offensive coordinator landed on the read-only defensive plan and had to switch to Offense to edit the install.
findings.expected: The scouting target and the staff member’s planning unit should be independently selectable.
findings.proposed_change: Preserve the coordinator’s planning unit separately from the opponent unit selected in scouting.
findings.quote: I study their defense because I call our offense.

keep: Keep the numerator, denominator, percentage and review-basis tag together on each scouting finding.
Keep late safety rotation in its own uncertain group with “too small to call” and the missing far-safety explanation.
Keep the film correction panel’s original formation, uncertainty, reviewer attribution and corrected value side by side.
Keep the eleven offense sections, v1/v2 selection, and the approved version’s approver and time on the plan.
Keep version- and section-specific comments and the explicit head-coach-only retention message.

verdict.condition: I would use scouting and draft comments alongside Hudl to verify film. I would not recommend this build for staff sign-off while Approve can discard a pending edit. I would reconsider when approval requires me to save that edit first, the approved version reopens with the objective I saw at sign-off, and I can trace each unit recommendation to playable snaps and record my decision.
